prompt.adult: Before the tempter came to Him, how long had Jesus fasted in the wilderness?
prompt.child: Jesus went without food in the wilderness before He was tempted. For how long?
prompt.teen: How long did Jesus fast in the wilderness before He was hungry and the tempter came?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 4:2, how long did Jesus fast before He was hungry?

verses.text: Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
And when He had fasted forty days and forty nights, afterward He was hungry.

explanation.adult: Matthew 4:2 tells how long Jesus fasted. Read the first half of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Matthew 4:2. It says how long Jesus fasted.
explanation.teen: Check the opening of Matthew 4:2 for the length of the fast.
explanation.older: Matthew 4:2 states the length of the fast, counting both days and nights, before noting that He was hungry.

teaching.extended_explanation: Matthew 4:1-2 says the Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness, where He fasted. The length is given in verse 2.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights in the wilderness.

prompt.adult: When the tempter first came to Jesus, what did he tell Him to turn into bread?
prompt.child: The tempter dared Jesus to make bread out of something. What was it?
prompt.teen: In the first temptation, what did the devil tell Jesus to command to become bread?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 4:3, what did the tempter tell Jesus to command to become bread?

verses.text: Now when the tempter came to Him, he said, “If You are the Son of God, command that these stones become bread.”

explanation.adult: Matthew 4:3 records the tempter's words. Look at what he told Jesus to command.
explanation.child: Read the words in quotation marks in Matthew 4:3.
explanation.teen: In Matthew 4:3, find what the tempter pointed to when he said "command that."
explanation.older: Matthew 4:3 gives the tempter's challenge word for word; notice what he wanted changed into bread.

teaching.extended_explanation: The tempter's first challenge in Matthew 4:3 was aimed at Jesus' hunger. Read what he wanted turned into bread.
teaching.takeaway: The tempter told Jesus to command stones to become bread.

prompt.adult: From an exceedingly high mountain, what did the devil show Jesus?
prompt.child: The devil took Jesus up a very high mountain. What did he show Him from there?
prompt.teen: What did the devil show Jesus, along with their glory, from the top of a high mountain?
prompt.older: According to Matthew 4:8, what did the devil show Jesus from an exceedingly high mountain?

choices.text: All the kingdoms of the world
All the stars and planets in the heavens

verses.text: Again, the devil took Him up on an exceedingly high mountain, and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
And he said to Him, “All these things I will give You if You will fall down and worship me.”

explanation.adult: Matthew 4:8 tells what the devil showed Jesus. Read the end of the verse.
explanation.child: Read the last part of Matthew 4:8.
explanation.teen: Look at the end of Matthew 4:8 for what was shown, along with its glory.
explanation.older: Matthew 4:8 names the mountain setting and then what the devil displayed, together with its glory.

teaching.extended_explanation: Matthew 4:8-9 describes a temptation on a high mountain. Verse 8 tells what the devil showed, and verse 9 tells what he asked in return.
teaching.takeaway: The devil showed Jesus all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.

prompt.adult: In Luke's account, Jesus said people do not live by bread alone. By what else do they live?
prompt.child: Jesus said people need more than bread to live. According to Luke 4:4, what else do they live by?
prompt.teen: When the devil tempted Him to make bread, Jesus said bread alone is not enough. What else did He name?
prompt.older: According to Luke 4:4, besides bread, by what does man live?

verses.text: But Jesus answered him, saying, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.’ ”

explanation.adult: Luke 4:4 quotes what is written. Read the words after "but by."
explanation.child: Read the end of Luke 4:4 to see what else people live by.
explanation.teen: Luke 4:4 finishes with the answer. Look at the last few words Jesus quoted.
explanation.older: In Luke 4:4 Jesus answers with what "is written"; the second half of the quotation names what man lives by besides bread.

teaching.extended_explanation: Jesus answered the devil from Scripture in Luke 4:4. Read the full quotation, especially its final words.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus said man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.

prompt.adult: After the people in the Nazareth synagogue grew angry and thrust Jesus out of the city, where did they lead Him?
prompt.child: The people in Jesus' hometown synagogue got angry and pushed Him out of town. Where did they take Him?
prompt.teen: The crowd in Nazareth drove Jesus out of the city. To what place did they lead Him?
prompt.older: According to Luke 4:29, where did the angry crowd in Nazareth lead Jesus?

choices.text: The bank of the Jordan River

verses.text: So all those in the synagogue, when they heard these things, were filled with wrath,
and rose up and thrust Him out of the city; and they led Him to the brow of the hill on which their city was built, that they might throw Him down over the cliff.
Then passing through the midst of them, He went His way.

explanation.adult: Luke 4:29 says where they led Jesus. Read the middle of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Luke 4:29 and look for where the crowd took Jesus.
explanation.teen: Luke 4:29 names the spot just before it says what they meant to do.
explanation.older: Luke 4:29 describes the crowd thrusting Him out of the city and then names the place on which their city was built.

teaching.extended_explanation: Luke 4:28-30 tells how the crowd reacted and how Jesus went His way. Verse 29 names where they led Him.
teaching.takeaway: The angry crowd led Jesus to the brow of the hill, but He passed through the midst of them.

prompt.adult: When John saw Jesus walking by, what did he call Him?
prompt.child: John looked at Jesus walking by and said something about Him. What did he call Jesus?
prompt.teen: Standing with two of his disciples, John pointed to Jesus. What did he call Him?
prompt.older: According to John 1:36, what did John call Jesus as He walked by?

verses.text: Again, the next day, John stood with two of his disciples.
And looking at Jesus as He walked, he said, “Behold the Lamb of God!”

explanation.adult: John 1:36 records John's words. Read what he said after "Behold."
explanation.child: Read the words in quotation marks in John 1:36.
explanation.teen: In John 1:36, look at the short exclamation John made.
explanation.older: John 1:36 gives John's exclamation as Jesus walked past; it is a single phrase following "Behold."

teaching.extended_explanation: In John 1:35-36 John is standing with two disciples when Jesus walks by. Read what he says in verse 36.
teaching.takeaway: John called Jesus "the Lamb of God."

prompt.adult: When Nathanael asked how Jesus knew him, where did Jesus say He had seen him before Philip called him?
prompt.child: Nathanael was surprised that Jesus knew him. Where did Jesus say He had seen Nathanael?
prompt.teen: Jesus amazed Nathanael by saying He had already seen him. Where was Nathanael at the time?
prompt.older: According to John 1:48, where did Jesus say He saw Nathanael before Philip called him?

verses.text: Nathanael said to Him, “How do You know me?” Jesus answered and said to him, “Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.”

explanation.adult: John 1:48 gives Jesus' answer to Nathanael. Read the end of the verse.
explanation.child: Read Jesus' words at the end of John 1:48.
explanation.teen: Look at the last part of John 1:48 for where Jesus saw Nathanael.
explanation.older: In John 1:48 Nathanael asks, "How do You know me?" Jesus' reply names the place where He saw him.

teaching.extended_explanation: Nathanael was amazed because Jesus knew where he had been before they met. Read Jesus' reply in John 1:48.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus said He saw Nathanael under the fig tree before Philip called him.

prompt.adult: In the Nazareth synagogue, Jesus read a passage about One anointed by the Spirit to preach the gospel to the poor. What did He then say about that passage?
prompt.child: In His hometown synagogue, Jesus read a promise about someone God would send. Then He sat down and spoke. What did He say about it?
prompt.teen: After Jesus read from the book of the prophet in Nazareth, He sat down with every eye on Him. What did He say about the words He had just read?
prompt.older: Reading Luke 4:18 and 4:21 together, what did Jesus declare about the Scripture He read in Nazareth?

choices.text: It was written only about King David
It would not come true for ages
It was too hard for them to understand
It was fulfilled that very day

verses.text: “The Spirit of the LORD is upon Me, Because He has anointed Me To preach the gospel to the poor; He has sent Me to heal the brokenhearted, To proclaim liberty to the captives And recovery of sight to the blind, To set at liberty those who are oppressed;
Then He closed the book, and gave it back to the attendant and sat down. And the eyes of all who were in the synagogue were fixed on Him.
And He began to say to them, “Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.”

explanation.adult: Luke 4:21 gives the first thing Jesus said after reading. Notice the first word of His statement.
explanation.child: Read Jesus' words in Luke 4:21. Look at when He said it was happening.
explanation.teen: Luke 4:20 sets the scene, and Luke 4:21 gives Jesus' statement. Pay attention to the timing in it.
explanation.older: Luke 4:18 is the passage Jesus read; Luke 4:21 is His claim about it. The opening word of that claim is the key.

teaching.extended_explanation: Jesus read words about the Spirit of the LORD resting on the One He anointed. In Luke 4:21 He told the synagogue how those words related to that moment. Read His sentence again.
teaching.takeaway: Jesus said, "Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing."
